distinctions_drawn: practice as aggregate vs. normative practice
following a rule vs. conforming to custom

dialectical_engagement.objection_handling: replies to conventionalism and relativism by distinguishing practice from mere consensus

method_and_evidence.evidence_type: conceptual analysis, ordinary language, musical examples, thought experiments

philosophical_orientation.sentiment: anti-essentialist but not anti-realist about rules
philosophical_orientation.thematic_focus: rule-following, family resemblance, normativity, meaning as use

summary_of_core_decisions: The text resolves the tension between rule-essence and rule-practice by rejecting the picture of a hidden essence and identifying rule-content with the grammar of use. It argues that rules are family-resemblance concepts, that understanding is a practical capacity to 'go on', and that examples and training are indispensable. It defends this view against conventionalism and relativism by emphasizing the normative, critical dimension internal to practices.
